reasons.specificity: The inventory maps eight named root metaphors (Vermögen as key, money as god, capital as machinery, myth-cycle, entrepreneur as prophet, etc.) to specific passages and authors in the text—Benjamin, Simmel, Marx, Schumpeter—rather than generic religion-economy themes, and the competing-frames table tracks the precise arguments those frames displace.
reasons.anchoring: Most quotes are verbatim and contextually accurate (e.g., 'the god of commodities,' 'option to have options,' 'generation-diffusion-institutionalization and decline,' 'keeps the capitalist machinery in motion'), though a few interpretations slightly over-schematize: the 'sign warning of the dog' analogy is cited correctly but labelled AN2 as having no limitation acknowledged when the text itself implicitly restricts it; and RM8's 'collective obsession' appears as the author's synthesis more than a developed mapping in the source.
reasons.non_obviousness: The analysis distinguishes the negative tertium comparationis strategy (paradox rather than a general concept of religion), identifies dead metaphors revived as logical problems (store of value, yardstick, medium), separates money-as-symbolic-medium from money-as-Vermögen as a structural fault line, and notes the phase-specificity of rationality—all points a casual reader of the abstract would miss.
reasons.coherence: Source attribution is consistent throughout prose, tables, and the findings ledger; the dominant-source-domain call (Religion) is supported by the cluster analysis; the competing-frames table aligns with the preference markings; and the counter-evidence section accurately records the text's self-qualifications without contradiction.
reasons.usefulness: The inventory gives a reader opening this dense text a navigable map: eight root metaphors with entailments and hidings, four competing framings with stakes and author preference, six analogies with effectiveness scores, eight dead metaphors, and 28 numbered findings—comprehensively covering what the article actually argues and enabling targeted reading.
reasons.hallucination_risk: No claims are invented that the text does not support; 'deus absconditus,' 'weaning off the drug,' 'the option to have options,' and 'prophets and priests' are all verbatim. The only slight risk is in EX4 labelling consultants as 'interpreters analogous to religious specialists'—the text mentions their role but does not itself deploy that analogy explicitly, though the priestly frame is developed nearby.

score.one_line: A thorough, source-anchored metaphor inventory that correctly identifies the religion cluster as load-bearing, accurately quotes and contextualizes the key mappings, and adds non-obvious distinctions (negative tertium, phase-specific rationality, Vermögen vs. medium) with only minor over-extension in a few analogies.
